description: We're Team Marscope, a group of explorers, coders, and designers building a map for the first humans on Mars. For the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge, we created an app that brings data from multiple sources into one layered view of the Martian surface, so astronauts can locate places, plan routes, and understand the terrain ahead. Marscope turns decades of NASA's robotic exploration data into a clear guide to help them get there quickly and safely.
summary: We developed MarsCope, an intelligent Martian exploration and survival map that consolidates essential planetary data into one accessible platform. Unlike terrestrial travel research that focuses on culture, preparing for Mars requires understanding critical survival factors—what to breathe, how to walk, and how not to freeze. MarsCope addresses this challenge by combining a 3D Mars globe with a detailed, interactive map of Jezero Crater built on accurate NASA data. Users can toggle six clearly labeled analytical layers—surface imagery, elevation, geology, thermal data, hazards, and routes—to analyze the terrain. This platform is important because successful exploration begins long before the first human footprint. By spotlighting key sites like the Crater Floor, Delta Front, and Crater Rim, MarsCope helps researchers and everyday learners investigate rock formation, ancient lake conditions, and planetary history to understand the ground beneath us.
details: MarsCope is an intelligent Martian exploration and survival map designed to centralize essential planetary data into a single, intuitive platform. Powered by accurate NASA datasets, it combines an interactive 3D Mars globe with a detailed map of Jezero Crater where users can toggle six clearly labeled analytical layers: surface imagery, elevation, geology, thermal observations, hazards, and routes. Creatively framed around the idea that preparing for Mars requires researching survival—what to breathe, how to walk, and how not to freeze—rather than earthly culture, the project makes complex planetary science accessible for daily learning and mission planning. By highlighting three key locations within Jezero Crater—the Crater Floor, Delta Front, and Crater Rim—MarsCope helps users investigate critical questions about rock formation, ancient lake environments, and planetary history before humans ever take their first step on the Martian surface. We mostly used our self intelligence and creativity to build as well as develop the application, however we also used the assistance and help from specialized AI.
